newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico retail leader sees recovery in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mexico retail leader sees recovery in 1997.

text.p: Mexican retail chains will see a gradual recovery next year, barring any unforeseen political or economic problems in the country, an industry leader said.

"If there are no surprises on the political and economic front, 1997 will be a year of recovery for the sector," said Luis Santana Castillo, chairman of the National Association of Self-Service and Department Stores, in an interview with Reuters late Thursday.
Santana said that self-service stores such as supermarkets had reined in the year-on-year drop in sales to four percent in June and July, compared to falls of 20 percent for both months in 1995.
"Department stores meanwhile chalked up (year-on-year) growth of two to three percent (in June and July)," he added, compared to falls of 40 percent for the same months last year.
Santana also complained of the sizeable losses incurred by the industry due to the hogh rate of robberies in department and self service stores.
Crime has rocketed in Mexico since the economic crisis following the December 1994 peso devaluation.

"Robberies arising from lack of public safety exceed the effectiveness of (anti-crime) measures taken by the businesses themselves. Although it is difficult to calculate amounts, they are at a high," he said, adding that the crime rate was "heavy and serious."
"Only security firms transporting funds from stores to banks have raised their fees by 100 percent since last year," he added.
-- Maria Luisa Aguilar, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9553
